relevance_note: Narrative review of ubiquitin-pathway autoinflammatory diseases that covers HA20 and gives individual-level detail for two patients from earlier reports, stating 'Zhou et al. reported 11 patients from 6 families' with 'haploinsufficiency of A20'.
method_note: Narrative review with no first-hand patients. All HA20 numbers are group counts in Table 2 (columns 'Patients (16) (n = 11)', 'Patients (37) (n = 6)', 'Patients (36) (n = 3)', 'Patients (35) (n = 1)'); per D-24 no count (e.g. '11/11' or '0/1') was used for any individual, in either direction (so even '11/11' oral ulcers did not make that item 'observed'), and the table legend defines '/' as 'not reported'. Several Table 2 cells hold more than one value in one cell ('1/3; 1/3', '0/6; 0/6; 1/6', '1/11; 4/11; 2/11'); these values are not labelled per patient, so they were left unassigned and no positional reading was attempted. Only two people are described with individual-level detail, both from earlier reports (refs (16) and (35)); labels follow rule 4: 'ref (16) patient' and 'ref (35) patient'. Variant rows are kept with 'not reported' because the review prints no variant description for either person. No contradictions found in the paper. I read the whole paper myself; no script transcribed any table. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null because the authors state no total; Table 2 tabulates HA20 cohorts of 11, 6, 3 and 1 patients without summing them. The normal CD3+CD8+ memory subpopulations of the ALPS patient are recorded as the ruled-out abnormality (D-27).
